rows.text: Submitted the "submit-comment" form at https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042 (the submission is public). Fields: "{\"name\":\"Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold\",\"organization\":\"Halcyon Threshold\",\"email\":\"morgan@halcyonthreshold.org\",\"comment\":\"We appreciate the opportunity to comment on the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting (FMIR) rule. This regulation addresses a critical gap in AI safety governance and could substantially improve outcomes. We submit the following feedback on key design questions.\\n\\n1. DEFINITION OF \\\"SERIOUS SAFETY INCIDENT\\\"\\nIssue: The rule references \\\"serious safety incidents\\\" but provides limited guidance on what constitutes this threshold. Clear definitions are essential for consistent reporting. Recommendation: Establish tiered incident classification (minor, moderate, serious, critical); provide concrete examples; include near-miss reporting for systematic learning; build in feedback mechanisms.\\n\\n2. 72-HOUR REPORTING TIMELINE\\nIssue: The timeline balances speed with accuracy, but implementation varies by incident type. Complex incidents may require investigation to understand severity. Recommendation: Distinguish between \\\"initial incident notification\\\" (24-48 hours, preliminary info) and \\\"full incident report\\\" (72-168 hours); require immediate notification of active safety risks; define what \\\"investigation\\\" means to prevent indefinite delays.\\n\\n3. INCIDENT DATA MANAGEMENT\\nIssue: How should incident reports be stored and analyzed to maximize learning while preventing misuse? Overly restricted access limits learning; public release enables exploitation. Recommendation: Establish tiered access (restricted for raw data, research access with NDA for de-identified patterns, public access for summaries); require annual meta-analysis; establish independent audit process.\\n\\n4. INTEGRATION WITH EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE\\nIssue: This rule should complement existing mechanisms rather than operate in isolation. Recommendation: Reference relationship to other safety standards; establish information-sharing with international partners; create feedback loops to inform model development; coordinate with existing reporting mechanisms.\\n\\n5. IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT\\nRecommendation: Publish comprehensive guidance; establish helpline for edge cases; support standardized classification schema; provide training for affected companies.\\n\\n6. EFFECTIVENESS METRICS\\nRecommendation: Establish metrics for coverage, timeliness, quality, utility, and adoption to evaluate if the rule is working.\\n\\nThe proposed FMIR rule addresses a genuine governance gap in frontier AI development. With attention to these design questions—particularly around definition clarity, implementation support, and data management—this rule can effectively improve AI safety outcomes. We recommend these refinements to maximize impact while remaining practical to implement.\"}"
